Disc’s other asset is a monoclonal antibody called DISC-0974 picked up from AbbVie upon the biotech’s launch in 2019. Earlier this year, Disc shared that the asset reduced hepcidin and increased iron levels for patients with myelofibrosis (MF) and anemia in a Phase 2 trial called RALLY-MF .
Additional data from RALLY-MF are slated to read out sometime this quarter and are expected to “further clarify the asset’s differentiated profile in myelofibrosis anemia, with end of Phase 2 discussions with FDA providing more details on future Ph 3 trial design,” according to a September report from BMO.
As for bitopertin, Disc said in its press release that an FDA decision is expected by mid-2027. Asked if, given the previous allocation of a CNPV, the agency might move faster than the six months typical for a resubmission, Quisel said it’s possible. “They have a lot of priorities, so we will certainly ask, and we’ll see what we get.”

It’s that time of the year when some of the carmakers playing the game on the American market are busy launching the refreshed versions of their products, dressed in new model-year clothes. Japanese Nissan is no exception, and announced this week the same for the Pathfinder range.
Unlike the competition, though, Nissan has a special reason to refresh this particular model: in 2027, just two months and some change from now, the nameplate celebrates its 40th year of existence. And that deserves a special edition model, which is exactly what Nissan has done.
Enter the 2027 Nissan Pathfinder Special Edition, a visual throwback to the original SUV of the late 1980s, but also a version with dedicated extras. Somehow, the Japanese carmaker managed to sneak the new model smack down in the middle of the lineup.
The so-called 2027 Nissan Pathfinder Special Edition slots between the SL FWD and the Platinum FWD, carrying a sticker that reads $47,390 for the front-wheel-drive, and $49,390 for the four-wheel drive.
For that cash, customers will get the same powertrain that’s available across the range, meaning the 3.5-liter V6 rated at 284 horsepower and 259 lb-ft of torque, tied to a nine-speed automatic transmission.
What makes it special is, first and foremost, the heritage-inspired styling and the unique interior appointments. There’s not that many of them to talk about, but carefully chosen as to mean something for the people with a passion for special editions.
It all starts inside, where Nissan went for a two-tone color scheme in black and burgundy and TailorFit materials designed to reference the cloth seating on the very first Pathfinder from 1987.
In the cabin, there are second-row captain’s chairs, with the rear doors fitted from the factory with sunshades. Finally, a Bose sound system with 12 speakers makes sure the occupants are entertained.
The bodywork of the SUV comes with red accents, and the word Pathfinder is featured on the liftgate. Making the connection with the ground are 20-inch alloy wheels in black, while the rear is adorned with a tow hitch receiver that takes the vehicle’s towing capacity to 6,000 pounds (2,722 kg).
There are, in all, nine Nissan Pathfinder models that can be had in 2027 model year guise. You can find them, prices included (minus $1,575 destination and handling), in the lines below. Before you do that, keep in mind that all of them will become available this November.

The organizers brought together Canadian and Andalusian mining representatives to explore investment and collaboration opportunities. Credit: C.McClelland
By: Colin McClelland in Seville October 19, 2026
The Andalucia region in Spain wants to attract mining investors with faster approvals and access to hundreds of areas covered by expired mineral rights, as Europe seeks the capacity to mine at least 10% of its annual consumption of strategic raw materials by 2030.
The southern region accounts for about 90% of the value of Spain’s metal mining and ranks second in the European Union for copper output, behind Poland, regional officials said Monday. Its producers include Atalaya Mining (LSE: ATYM), which operates the Cerro Colorado open pit in the Riotinto district of Huelva province.
“Last year we got the permitting of a new mine from the beginning in just 27 months,” Jesús Portillo García-Pintos, the region’s director-general for sustainable mining and raw materials science, told an international mining forum in Seville. “Twenty-seven months in the mining sector is a dream, we know.”
Andalucia’s pitch extends beyond opening mines: officials want investors to process more minerals locally, develop mining technology and create skilled jobs that help retain the region’s graduates. Faster permits and public funding are intended to turn its mineral wealth into a broader industrial base as Europe seeks to reduce its reliance on imported raw materials.
Targets
The EU’s mining capacity already covered about 8% of its strategic raw-material consumption when the targets were set, European auditors estimated in a 2026 report , using 2016–2020 data. That aggregate masks deeper shortfalls in materials such as natural graphite and rare earths.
Even with faster approvals, meeting Europe’s 2030 goals will be difficult, Portillo acknowledged when questioned about the timetable. Developing processing industries could be easier than opening new mines, he said, although both present challenges.
Andalucia had 73 active exploration permits as of August. It put more than 450 expired mining rights out to tender across its eight provinces in 2025, Portillo said. The region has nearly 480 active mines and quarries.
A dedicated government unit coordinates departments to accelerate project approvals. Investors can also consult geological maps, mineral-rights information and other technical material through the government’s mining portal .
Incentives
Andalucia has earmarked €40 million (C$63.2 million) in mining incentives covering innovation in exploration, mineral processing and waste treatment, alongside energy efficiency.
Improving geological knowledge of both deposits and historical mining waste is another priority, including through cooperation with Spain’s geological survey, Portillo said.
“We have to strengthen this knowledge, not only about the primary resources, but also the secondary resources, the wastes,” he said. “Andalucia has a substantial mining past so in the wastes, we have a big body that we can provide.”
Andalucia assumed leadership in January of S3P Mining Regions, a European Commission-backed partnership promoting innovation and cooperation among mining areas.
The partnership now spans seven countries following Poland’s addition in September, Portillo said. Alongside Spain, the other participants are Finland, Sweden, France, Portugal and Greece. Cooperation connects regions with strong mining operations to those with more developed processing industries and technology.
Mines, processing
Much of Andalucia’s metal mining is concentrated in the Iberian Pyrite Belt, which extends across southwestern Spain into Portugal. Existing plants, ports and engineering suppliers provide infrastructure for further development.
Atalaya’s Riotinto plant can process 15 million tonnes annually. The company aims to use it as a regional processing hub, with Masa Valverde, San Dionisio and San Antonio among its surrounding deposits.
Sandfire Resources (ASX: SFR) owns the MATSA complex , also in Huelva. Its Aguas Teñidas, Magdalena and Sotiel underground mines feed a central plant with annual capacity of 4.7 million tonnes, producing copper and zinc concentrates with lead and silver byproducts.
The EU’s ambitions extend downstream, with 2030 benchmarks for domestic capacity to process 40% and recycle 25% of the union’s annual strategic raw-material consumption.
Near Seville, Cobre Las Cruces illustrates the processing investment officials want to attract. Global Panduro, controlled by Resource Capital Funds, acquired the business from First Quantum Minerals (TSX: FM) in June.
The new owner is advancing an underground mine and refinery designed to produce copper, zinc, lead and silver. The European Commission designated the development a strategic project in March 2025 under its critical raw materials act.
Atlantic Copper, owned by Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX), inaugurated its CirCular plant in Huelva in September. It is designed to process up to 60,000 tonnes of electrical and electronic equipment annually, recovering copper and other metals.
Training for growth
The region’s education system is another draw for investors, said Elena Gallego, head of the Invest in Andalucía department at regional business agency Andalucía Trade.
Andalucia has 15 universities educating about 250,000 students and roughly 900 vocational training centres, according to figures presented at the forum and published by Spain’s investment promotion agency.
Universities and vocational centres work with companies to tailor training to their equipment, technologies and staffing needs, Gallego said. Her investment service helps companies select sites, find staff and establish operations.
“We have always been a net exporter of talent in the region,” she said. “We did not have enough opportunities for all the professionals coming out of these universities to stay in the region.” Attracting investment could help bring some of those workers home, she added.
Manuel Sevilla Ramos, director of the Centre of Excellence and Innovation for Sustainable Mining, an initiative of Spanish metal mining association Aminer, said the opportunity extends beyond extraction.
“The real challenge is to build around our resources a value chain capable of generating knowledge, innovation, jobs, technology, and industrial security,” he said.
The centre connects companies, universities and researchers on issues including water management, digitalization, safety and training.
Canadian connection
Canada’s Mining Innovation Commercialization Accelerator, or MICA , is exploring how Canadian technology suppliers could work with Spanish operators and how Spanish innovations could serve the projects it supports.
The federally funded C$45-million initiative, managed by the Sudbury-based Centre for Excellence in Mining Innovation, has funded 75 innovation projects and helped bring 24 technologies to mine-site pilots, said Lorelei Ratushniak, its director of mining relations.
Her presentation proposed a demonstration at an Iberian operation or a joint Canada–Spain mining challenge in 2027.
“I’m very excited to see some of the challenges and opportunities from colleagues that presented this morning, particularly around waste,” Ratushniak said. “That is a great opportunity as we have a lot of technologies within that area, and again, we focus across the entire mining life cycle.”
Portillo identified access to mine sites for testing new technologies as another gap the region needs to address.

By [email protected]
19 October 2026
Solar energy is becoming increasingly important for bolstering sub-Saharan Africa’s trading potential, with supply chain executives telling The Loadstar that Kenya and Nigeria are two of the fastest-growing markets for the technology.
By the end of the first quarter, Nigeria had climbed into the top 10 of solar panel suppliers to the US, with some 40% of the country’s total exports of the technology, totalling $64bn, ending up in the US.
That growth has been felt by forwarders and logistics partners. DHL Express’s chief executive for Sub-Saharan Africa, Hennie Heymans, told The Loadstar the company was seeing “incredible growth” in solar-panel exports out of Nigeria – and nor is that country alone.
“We actually see an incredible growth in solar panel exports towards the United States from Nigeria and Kenya,” he said, pointing out that for Africa in general the “new energy” vertical was proving something of a winner, experiencing 20% growth year on year.
Interestingly, local forwarders told The Loadstar solar panels were also proffering volumes in the reverse direction for Kenya, although there was debate around whether the volumes were part of a local redevelopment of energy infrastructure or the result of chaos in the supply chains.
One forwarder told The Loadstar that, amid the situation in Hormuz and growing pockets of congestion at typical transhipment hubs, volumes were routing via Kenya in an effort to avoid being caught up in the chaos.
Mr Heymans, however, believes the growth in solar typifies the present story across Africa, noting that DHL had experienced a recent uptick in enquiries about special economic zones (SEZs) in several African countries, particularly Kenya and South Africa.
Without stating just how many SEZ-related enquiries his office had handled, Mr Heymans said: “In Kenya, we have seen interest focused specifically on Mombasa, as well as Nairobi, and we have seen new entrants in both locations.”
And he is not alone in noting this: businesses the world over are reassessing international supply chains amid geopolitical tension and changing trade policies, with growing indications that the continent is more than well suited as a base for production.

DHL Group revised upward its profit forecast for 2026, pointing to ongoing earnings strength at its express division and expectations of a “robust” peak shipping season that coincides with holiday sales.
The global logistics giant said Friday it now expects earnings before interest and taxes to exceed 7 billion euros (equivalent to $7.8 billion), topping its earlier outlook for $7.3 billion from core operations.
DHL Group ( XETRA: DHL ) also raised its full-year projection for free cash flow to $3.6 billion from $3.37 billion earlier. Capital expenditures are expected to rise to about $4 billion, up from about $3.4 billion to $3.7 billion as DHL invests in projects for further growth.
The company announced last week, for example, that it plans to invest $450 million to expand capabilities in Central and Eastern Europe by 2030.
Group EBIT during the third quarter reached $1.92 billion, up 16% year over year and above the consensus estimate by analysts. DHL Express led the way with adjusted operating profit increasing 49.5% to $1.16 billion on the strength of higher yield, continued cost efficiencies and a more disciplined approach towards accepting heavy airfreight, which commands higher rates, over lightweight shipments transported by the company’s in-house airline. Heavyweight air has been a point of emphasis for the company this year. The tight air freight market also boosted results.
DHL Global Forwarding also performed well, generating EBIT of $292 million, up a third from the prior year, excluding small one-time effects in 2025. Earnings at DHL Supply Chain, the contract logistics unit, increased 7.9% to $337 million on an adjusted basis.
DHL eCommerce had adjusted operating profit of $56.2 million, down from $198 million in the third quarter of 2025. The prior year benefitted from a one-time $138.2 million gain.
Operating profit at Post & Parcel Germany declined 32% to $168.5 million.
Full third-quarter results are scheduled to be released on Nov. 5.

Pennsylvania is putting $371.5 million into the Port of Philadelphia, a move state officials say will unlock hundreds of millions more and launch the largest expansion in the port ’s history.
What’s Related
Gov. Josh Shapiro and PennDOT Secretary Mike Carroll announced the state funding last week at PhilaPort. The state money is expected to bring in another $466 million, including more than $200 million in private investment and $266 million in federal grants. All told, the growth plan is valued at more than $837 million.
“This is a game changer for PhilaPort,” Shapiro said.
The state expects the plan to create more than 6,000 new jobs and generate $45 million in state and local taxes. It’s also projected to grow the port’s container capacity by 122% and its auto capacity by 18%.
RELATED: Top 30 U.S. Ports Ranked By Container Imports In 2025
Breakdown of where money is going
The state’s $371.5 million breaks down into four main pieces:
$31 million for dredging at Southport Berth I
$145 million for reclamation at Southport Berth II and the North Wharf
$109.4 million for land acquisition
$58.1 million for cranes and equipment
Two U.S. Department of Transportation grants will help build a new 2,000-linear-foot berth at the Southport Marine Terminal, the port’s first new berth in 50 years. The plan also includes buying the 152-acre Mustin Yard parcel, upgrading the Tioga Marine Terminal berth to handle liquid bulk barges and breakbulk vessels, and buying and developing more property in the Southern Port District.
More room for cars and containers
“PhilaPort is critical to Pennsylvania’s transportation network, connecting global trade to local communities,” Carroll said.
Port partners say the extra space is what they’ve been waiting for. Scott Cornell, CEO of GLOVIS America, said, “As the world’s largest ocean carrier of finished vehicles, we needed to match with best-in-class terminal capacity.”
Leo Holt, president of Holt Logistics , called the project “a job multiplier that will go on for the better part of a decade.”
“Governor Shapiro’s continued investment in PhilaPort will help us expand operations,” said Rich Lazer, CEO and executive director of PhilaPort, adding that “our future has never been brighter.”
The most productive container port in the U.S.
The World Bank has named PhilaPort the most productive container port in the U.S. for three years running. In 2025, the port was responsible for more than 8,000 jobs and nearly $1.2 billion in economic output in Pennsylvania.
The state has put more than $600 million into the port over the past decade. Recent projects include about $10 million from PennDOT for a new intersection at the Packer Avenue Marine Terminal, where construction started in January, and $11 million over two years from the Department of General Services for maintenance dredging.

Chevrolet's Japan-Market Corvette V8 Tourer Special Edition Is Limited to Merely 15 Units
8 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
For an extra 1.9 million yen over the current Stingray for Japan, the V8 Tourer comes with brighter wheels, different seats, and no extra power from its already discontinued powertrain. Boasting a very coherent red, silver, and tan aesthetic, the limited-run model is coming to Japanese dealers from 21.5 million yen.
That's 135,750 freedom eagles at current exchange rates, and only 15 units are in the offing nationwide. Just under 10 percent more expensive than the Stingray convertible, the V8 Tourer wants you to enjoy looking at it, sitting at it, and driving it rather than explain your purchase in more rational terms.
Instead of black, the retractable roof panel, nacelles behind the seats, A pillars, and side intake trim pieces all match the Red Mist Metallic Tincoat body panels. By default, Chevrolet Japan ships the Stingray convertible with Carbon Flash touches. Bringing those surfaces into the body color obviously changes the look of the car, especially with the roof closed, when the red no longer stops at the cabin's edge.
Silver is there to supply the contrast, beginning with full-length Sterling Silver dual racing stripes. Chrome emblems are on the menu as well, making for a hardly anonymous combination. The lighter strips and dark-ish red work amazingly well, doing their jobs perfectly without fighting each other for the spotlight.
The wheels also help, for Chevrolet Japan chose Pearl Nickel forged aluminum rollers rather than Midnight Gray wheels. The design also differs, with the Pearl Nickel units rocking five split spokes instead of twenty spokes for the Grays. Black calipers are featured as well, and the visual drama continues with a familiar low-profile rear spoiler.
Photo: Chevrolet What Chevy refers to as Natural Dipped is the color that dominates the interior, where you will find Natural seatbelts and GT2 bucket seats. Limited-edition ornaments on the floor mats and passenger side are listed as well, yet the GT2 buckets are the real stars here, replacing the standard Competition Sport seats.
GT2s blend comfort, a sporting appearance, carbon-fiber trim, and Nappa leather upholstery. Just like the Stingray convertible, the V8 Tourer also benefits from Magnetic Selective Ride Control dampers. The Z51 go-faster package is understandably featured as well, bringing forth an electronic limited-slip differential, better cooling, larger brakes, and so forth.
Under the hood, you will find the LT2 small block that General Motors recently discontinued in the US-market Corvette for the LS6. The newcomer isn't only larger, but also breathes differently because GM finally made a case for dual injection to the detriment of direct-only injection for the LT2.
Rated at 495 horsepower and 470 pound-feet (637 Newton-meters), the V8 Tourer only comes in right-hand drive. Its folding roof can be operated at speeds no higher than 30 miles per hour, which is nearly 50 clicks in metric speak. A standard front lift raises the nose roughly 1.6 inches (40 millimeters) in three seconds, and that makes a world of difference when the car meets a steep driveway.
Scheduled to arrive in customers' hands from November 2026, the V8 Tourer is backed by a three-year/60,000-kilometer warranty. Of course, Chevrolet Assist 24/7 roadside assistance is included for additional peace of mind.

By Alex Lennane
19 October 2026
Higher EU parcel charges could further strengthen the case for retailers to hold stock in Europe, as reduced China–Europe freighter capacity and elevated airfreight rates add to the cost pressures facing cross-border supply chains.
An additional €2 EU handling fee per product category is expected from 1 November, on top of the €3 customs duty introduced in July on qualifying consignments worth €150 or less.
For a parcel containing three product categories, the combined charges would reach €15 before transport, clearance, and VAT costs. The handling fee would also apply to orders above €150, although those shipments face normal customs tariffs rather than the temporary €3 duty.
The changes could alter the calculation for brands choosing between shipping individual consumer orders from outside the EU and importing inventory for subsequent local fulfilment.
Robert Jeffrey, senior advisor for international structuring at Dutch advisory firm Holdwise, told The Loadstar there was no evidence yet of brands switching.
“It is a little early to see brands switch. The €3 duty started on 1 July, and the €2 fee is expected from 1 November. We expect the first changes when brands plan their stock for next year.”
That planning comes against a backdrop of constrained freighter capacity between China and Europe.
Rotate data shows capacity on the trade down 20% year on year between 18 September and 18 October. Although capacity rebounded 27% last week, compared with the previous week, following China’s Golden Week holiday, it remained 24% below the equivalent week last year.
Meanwhile, WorldACD reported that global spot rates held, at $3.55 per kg, in the week ending 11 October, despite worldwide tonnage declining 1% in a third consecutive weekly fall.
Global volumes were, nevertheless, 9% above the equivalent week last year, while capacity was around 1% higher, and spot rates were up 34%. WorldACD attributed elevated rates to continuing capacity disruption and substantially higher jet fuel costs and associated surcharges.
Those figures illustrate the wider transport cost pressures on retailers’ distribution decisions.
Holdwise provided an illustrative comparison, involving a €90 consumer order containing a Chinese-made T-shirt and watch, bought by the brand for €30. Shipping the order directly from outside the EU would incur €6 in customs duty and an expected €4 handling fee. Adding assumed postage and clearance costs of €7, plus €2.50 for storage, picking and packing, produces a total of €19.50.
Under its alternative model, the brand imports unsold stock into the Netherlands by sea. Holdwise calculated €2 in normal customs duty, 50 cents per order for allocated freight and clearance, €2.50 for warehouse fulfilment and €5 for delivery within the EU: a total of €10.
The illustrative (and assumed) saving of €9.50 per order would amount to €190,000 across 20,000 annual orders.
Bulk replenishment does not necessarily mean abandoning airfreight: the transport mode would remain a separate commercial decision.
Crucially, consolidating existing consumer orders into one shipment does not remove the charges.
“The comparison is for stock that the Dutch company buys and clears at import, before it sells the goods,” Mr Jeffrey explained. Where goods have already been sold to consumers and are then shipped together, the individual orders remain subject to the relevant charges.
The handling fee’s precise start date also remains uncertain. Mr Jeffrey said the delegated regulation setting its amount was still subject to scrutiny and publication, making the change “expected from 1 November”.

Ford Order Guide Confirms 2027 Ranger Drops 2.7L EcoBoost V6, Detuned 3.0L EcoBoost V6 Replaces It
28 photos
Photo: Ford / edited
Ford is giving Ranger buyers a good reason to skip the Raptor entirely. As per the 2027 order guide, the XLT and Lariat are dropping the optional 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6 for the 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 that has already replaced the 2.7 in the mechanically similar Bronco and the F-150 pickup truck.
The order guide does not offer any kind of maximum output numbers for the newcomer, although the Bronco's advertised figures are believed to carry over. In optimal conditions, the detuned version of the Raptor's engine makes a very respectable 380 horsepower and 440 pound-feet (597 Newton-meters) of twist. Similarly, a 10-speed automatic tranny will have to suffice.
If the Ranger follows the Bronco's lead , the 3.0-liter EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 would amount to more than 0.3 additional liters of displacement. Against the outgoing 2.7, the 3.0 gives the midsizer an extra 65 horsepower and 40 pound-feet (54 Newton-meters) at full chatter, making the XLT a very appealing yet understated truck.
You wouldn't need the higher equipment group, either. Attached below, the order guide lists the new sixer for both the 300A and 301A groups, along with the Lariat's 500A specification. Four-wheel drive comes with the 3.0 by default, whereas the 2.3 remains the standard choice across the XLT and Lariat. XL buyers stick with four cylinders, though, as expected from a work-oriented trim level.
The XLT's 301A equipment group includes power adjustments for both front seats, heated front seats, and a power-sliding rear window. The guide further leaves room to build the sort of pickup that interests prospective customers who read a vehicle past wheel finishes and the paint job. Add the FX4 package, and you get an electronic locking rear diff, off-road shocks, a steel bash plate, and extra underbody protection.
Photo: Ford FX4 also sweetens the deal with Mud/Ruts and Sand drive mods, and the finishing touch is Trail Control. New optional rocker rails with hoop-style steps require the FX4 package. All in all, that combo gives the larger V6 a very tasteful supporting cast without pretending that lesser Rangers have turned into undercover Raptors.
Raptor customers are presented with trick dampers from the folks at Fox, locking front and rear axles, a nicer rear suspension setup, and Baja mode for good measure. Lariat and lesser models retain rear leaf springs in lieu of the Raptor's Watts-link design. The coil-sprung rear suspension of the Raptor improves high-speed stability off the beaten path and suspension travel, the trade-offs being maximum payload and towing capacities.
The order guide clearly states the Raptor's engine is a high-output affair, but even though it develops more than 400 ponies on premium-grade dinosaur juice, the Raptor-grade mill makes the very same 440 pound-feet of peak torque as the detuned 3.0 of non-Raptor grades. The cheapest Ranger for 2027 in the US market adds dual-zone electronic climate control, a 12-inch center display, Intersection Assist, and Lane Keeping Assist as standard.
Ford's Connectivity Package is standard as well, and it includes a one-year subscription. Ford Co-Pilot360 2.0 becomes standard on the XLT. No fewer than five optional packages have been deleted for 2027. In their place, Ford offers the Bronze Appearance Package, a graphics delete for said package, a graphics delete for the Black Appearance Package, and the Luxury Package.
The 17-inch black steelies are gone in favor of aluminum wheels. When it comes to paint options, Neptune Blue enters the scene to the detriment of Velocity Blue and Carbonized Gray. Lastly, the Space Gray interior theme replaces Sandstone.

Huawei’s smart car business is signing on to CATL’s battery swap network, giving the world’s largest battery maker another heavyweight partner for a technology most of the industry wrote off a decade ago.
Yinwang, the Huawei-controlled automotive unit also known as Newcool, signed a strategic cooperation framework with CATL and its swap subsidiary CAES on Monday. CATL’s Choco-swap network already counts 2,520 stations across about 200 Chinese cities.
What Huawei and CATL agreed to
According to Yinwang’s statement, reported by Reuters , the deal covers both swappable battery packs and the station network. CATL says the focus is on vehicles running Huawei’s Qiankun smart driving systems, which would be made compatible with Choco stations.
The new partnership is betting heavily on automation. CATL wants to link the car, the station and the cloud so the vehicle works out when it needs energy, based on its battery status and the driver’s habits, then finds a station, drives in on its own and lines itself up for the swap. CATL quotes 99 seconds for the swap itself.

CATL chairman Robin Zeng and Jin Yuzhi, Huawei senior vice president and Yinwang CEO, attended the signing.
The new partnership looks serious, but the announcement left out a few key details. No vehicle models, launch date or service areas were announced. It’s a framework agreement, and those don’t always turn into products.
Who’s behind Yinwang? Huawei owns 80% of it, with Seres and Changan’s Avatr holding 10% each. Seres builds AITO, the premium SUV brand Huawei’s software and retail network helped turn into a hit in China, and plenty of other Chinese automakers buy Huawei’s Qiankun systems.
More than 200 new swap stations a month
CATL first entered the battery swap market in 2022 with its EVOGO service, then relaunched the effort as Choco-swap around standardized packs at the end of 2024.
The growth since has been fast. Choco-swap ended 2025 with 1,020 stations, passed 2,000 at the start of July, and hit 2,520 as of September 29. As we reported this summer, CATL is building more than 200 battery swap stations every month . It’s aiming for more than 3,000 by the end of the year and 30,000 long term.
Huawei joins a growing list of Choco partners that includes GAC, BAIC and NIO. CATL is also pushing swapping for heavy trucks, including a joint venture with Octopus Energy for the UK and Europe .
For comparison, NIO, which built the first big swap network on its own, hit its 100 millionth swap in February with 3,790 stations. It passed 110 million swaps by June.
Electrek’s Take
I’ve been skeptical of battery swapping for years, and I had good reasons to be.
Tesla demoed a 90-second pack swap in 2013, opened a single pilot station at Harris Ranch in California, and quietly let it fade after owners showed little interest. Better Place raised about $850 million and still went bankrupt in 2013. And every year, chargers got faster, which shrank the one real advantage swapping had.
My main argument was standardization. Swapping only works as infrastructure if lots of automakers share packs, and automakers don’t want to share the most expensive part of the car. NIO proved swapping can work for one brand. But one brand’s network is a perk, not infrastructure.
CATL is the one company that can fix that problem, and it’s actually doing it. It supplies roughly 40% of the world’s EV battery cells, so when it shows up with a standard pack, automakers listen. 2,520 stations in under two years isn’t a pilot.
And Huawei brings autonomy. A car that drives itself into a station and leaves 99 seconds later doesn’t need anyone to plug it in. For robotaxis and commercial fleets, that solves a real problem.
I still don’t think swapping replaces charging. Most EV owners charge at home, and the fastest chargers in China are now getting close to gas station times. So it’s a complement. But I’m surprised to be writing this: in China, battery swapping is starting to look like a permanent part of the EV mix rather than a gimmick.
Will anyone build something like this outside of China?

Industry giant Ceva Logistics on Friday announced that it has merged France-focused last-mile delivery subsidiary Colis Privé into newly acquired Paack, which operates a dense delivery network in Spain and Portugal, presenting a single brand identity to the market.
Ceva Logistics, a top-five global logistics company by gross revenue and part of Marseilles, France-based CMA CGM Group, acquired Paack in early August to expand its last-mile delivery business in Europe. It acquired Colis Privé, which also operates in Belgium and Luxembourg, in 2022.
The unified Paack brand will be rolled out progressively to customers and partners beginning in January, Ceva said in a news release. When the tentative deal was first announced last summer, the expectation was that Colis Privé would absorb Paack.
The combined business delivers 150 million parcels annually through a network of 17,000 out-of-home delivery points — 8,000 each in France and Spain, and 1,500 in Belgium. Paack has about 490 employees. It also operates six urban delivery stations in France. The couriers also deliver to individual residences.
Uniting the Colis Privé and PAACK networks will simplify delivery management for e-commerce retailers operating across multiple European markets and provide a more consistent delivery experience for local and international packages, Ceva said.
One of Paack’s strong points is its sophisticated technology suite. Ceva previously said
Paack’s technology will immediately enhance Colis Privé’s capabilities in end-to-end parcel planning, real-time tracking, precise time-slot management, advanced reporting, integrated returns management and route optimization that minimizes delays.
Why It Matters: The e-commerce logistics sector in Europe is in a period of consolidation as companies look to expand delivery footprints and quickly access new markets to support the fast-growing online shopping market. Research firm ECDB estimates the e-commerce revenue in Europe will grow 36% in the second half of the decade, surpassing $1 trillion in 2029. Online retail sales are projected to grow 8.6% this year, on par with global growth. Portugal is the seventh fastest growing market at 9.1%.
Europe’s e-commerce market is enabled by a strong and expanding digital infrastructure, high internet penetration and a steadily growing base of online shoppers, ECDB said in a white paper this year. The online share of total retail sales in Europe is 18.2%, which is below the global average of 25%, and will increase to 18.7% by 2027.
The Paack-Colvis Privé combination fits with CMA CGM’s strategy of becoming an integrated, end-to-end logistics service provider , relying on a mix of its own air, ocean, truck, and parcel delivery assets, as well as third-party transportation providers. Having its own e-commerce logistics network allows Ceva Logistics to better control the delivery experience for B2C retailers from origin to customer.

The California-based defense company Shield AI said this week that its Hivemind software helped Honeywell Aerospace achieve autonomous flight after six weeks of training, down from an estimated 54 weeks, ahead of two flight demonstrations, according to Monday’s joint statement .
“Hivemind Enterprise handled the autonomy basics, so [Honeywell engineers] could spend its time on its own detection and tracking model,” said Tom Schaefer, vice president of Hivemind Enterprise at Shield AI. “We built Hivemind so partners can work this way.”
The companies announced their collaboration in July along with a memorandum of understanding , stating their goal was to help “defense operators move from demonstration to deployment faster… without having to rebuild confidence in each new system every time.”
Shield AI explained the Hivemind software provides “core capabilities such as route planning, mission management, and communication between aircraft,” so companies like Honeywell could integrate “their own AI models, sensors, and mission capabilities and [advance] them from simulation to flight.”
According to the statement, Honeywell’s autonomy team began training on Hivemind in late April and by mid-June, they flew a BFD-SE8 multirotor aircraft autonomously for the first time using the newly developed autonomy stack.
The team held the official demonstration on July 8 in Plymouth, Minnesota, where the aircraft took off on its own, followed a planned route, re-routed around a no-fly zone, and returned to base.
Afterward, the company said, the team immediately began working on the second demonstration. For three months, they trained and deployed their own target detection and tracking model.
On Oct. 8, the team hosted another demonstration in which a scout aircraft used the AI model to detect, identify, and track a target. It then passed the information to another aircraft, which navigated autonomously to the target, delivered a payload, and then returned to base with the scout.
Todd Giles, Honeywell Aerospace’s senior vice president of engineering and chief technology officer, credited “open architectures” — or the use of public standards for software development — for “changing the pace of innovation in aerospace” and his team’s accomplishment.
“By combining our expertise in avionics, navigation, sensing, and autonomy, we are helping create a scalable foundation for the next generation of autonomous aircraft and mission systems,” Giles said.

Foxconn is buying half of Mitsubishi Electric’s auto parts business for ¥115 billion ($727 million), its biggest bet yet on turning years of EV promises into a real car business.
But the target, Mitsubishi Electric Mobility, isn’t an EV company. It’s a traditional Tier 1 supplier that makes everything from alternators and ignition coils to radar sensors, with a smaller electric powertrain business attached.
Hon Hai Precision Industry, Foxconn’s formal name, announced on Friday that its investment arm, Lin Yin International Investment, signed a final agreement to take a 50% stake in the Mitsubishi Electric subsidiary. The two companies will run it as an equal joint venture.
The deal values the business at ¥320 billion ($2 billion) in enterprise value and ¥230 billion in equity value. Closing is expected on October 1, 2027, after antitrust reviews.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The pitch: Japanese EV platforms
The partners want to combine Mitsubishi Electric’s electric powertrain, software and vehicle control technology with Foxconn’s “speed and scale” to develop EV platforms in Japan. They plan to sell them to Japanese automakers first, then globally under a “Made in/by Japan” banner.
They’re targeting more than ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) in revenue for the fiscal year starting April 2030.
Jun Seki, Foxconn’s EV chief strategy officer and a former Nissan executive, told reporters that Mitsubishi’s electronic control technology was “the most attractive thing” about the deal. He said Foxconn wants to make Mitsubishi Electric “our anchor in Japan and team up with other parts makers and automakers.”
Foxconn is buying a parts supplier, not an EV platform
Mitsubishi Electric spun its automotive equipment group into Mitsubishi Electric Mobility in April 2024. Before closing, it will fold the rest of its car business, including the automotive operations of its overseas subsidiaries, into the unit. That combined business is what Foxconn is buying into.
Here’s what’s in Mitsubishi Electric’s automotive catalog :
Charging and starting: alternators, starters and motor generators
Engine and transmission: gasoline engine control units, ignition coils, fuel pump modules, turbo and variable valve timing actuators, EGR valves, transmission control units and a long list of sensors
Steering: electric power steering motors and controllers
Driver assistance: millimeter-wave radar, forward cameras, ADAS control units and driver monitoring systems
Body electronics: smart entry, immobilizers and airbag control units
Electrification: traction motors, inverters, battery management units, EV control units and on-board chargers
Mitsubishi Electric doesn’t break out revenue by product line. But its May 2025 strategy presentation points to “large market share” in rotary motors (alternators and starters) and car mechatronics, and says it runs its EV and combustion engine businesses “in a balanced way.” It’s already exiting car multimedia and fuel injectors, and it handed its lighting business to Stanley Electric. In July, the unit said it was reviewing its combustion engine business as EV demand slowed.
And the business is shrinking. It brought in ¥875.6 billion ($5.5 billion) in revenue and ¥54.4 billion in operating profit, a 6.2% margin, in the fiscal year that ended in March. That’s down ¥43.5 billion from the year before, which Mitsubishi Electric blamed on weaker sales by Japanese automakers in China and a smaller car multimedia business in North America. It expects ¥820 billion this year.
So the ¥1 trillion goal works out to roughly 5% growth a year. For a deal sold as an EV play, that’s modest.
No chips, and a discount price
Foxconn isn’t getting Mitsubishi Electric’s power semiconductors. The SiC and IGBT power modules that go inside EV inverters belong to a separate power device business, which Mitsubishi Electric put into merger talks with Rohm and Toshiba in March. The Foxconn deal covers the automotive equipment business only.
It isn’t getting a proven EV components partnership either. Mitsubishi Electric Mobility and Aisin agreed in May 2024 to form a joint venture for traction motors, inverters and control software. Five months later, they scrapped the JV and downgraded it to a business alliance.
Then there’s the price. The ¥320 billion enterprise value is about 0.37 times sales and roughly six times operating profit. The ¥230 billion equity value is also well below the roughly ¥352 billion in net assets on the business’s books (¥727.5 billion in assets minus ¥375.4 billion in liabilities), which is why Mitsubishi Electric expects to book a ¥100 billion impairment this fiscal year.
That’s not how anyone prices a growth business. Mitsubishi Electric is selling down a mature, low-margin division, much like Panasonic did when it sold a majority of its automotive systems unit to Apollo in 2024.
Foxconn’s EV track record
Foxconn has been talking big about EVs for six years. In October 2020, chairman Young Liu said the company wanted to supply components or services for 10% of the world’s EVs, around 3 million vehicles, sometime between 2025 and 2027.
Since then, it has unveiled a series of Foxtron prototypes , bought the former GM plant in Lordstown, Ohio, and lined up the Fisker Pear , and added a pickup and a crossover to the lineup. Fisker went bankrupt in 2024 and the Pear never made it to production. Foxconn sold the Lordstown factory last year for $375 million.
It also approached Nissan about a stake in early 2025, as the Honda-Nissan merger talks collapsed. Nothing came of it.
So far, the only legacy automaker to put its badge on a Foxtron-developed EV is Mitsubishi Motors, a separate company from Mitsubishi Electric. Its ASX VR-e, built by Yulon in Taiwan, is going on sale in Australia and New Zealand. Foxconn also has a bus joint venture with Mitsubishi Fuso and is a partner in Saudi Arabia’s Ceer EV brand.

GM just took the wraps off the electric-drive pickup America’s commercial fleets have been waiting for: a one-ton chassis, dually rear axle and massive capability baked in. The best part? You can have it in any color you want — as long as it’s Army green.
Officially dubbed the UGV, the newly revealed Unmanned Ground Vehicle is a cab-less, autonomous machine built on what GM is calling, “the dual-rear-wheel Chevy Silverado 3500 HD skateboard architecture,” the UGV is being developed to support military operations with silent (read: electric) logistics and casualty evacuation.
The most significant takeaway, however, is that GM has developed an extended-range electric 3500 pickup chassis – and it may be Army-crawling its way to production .
Wishful thinking
Silverado EV towing; via Kendall Chevrolet.
GM’s official press release on the UGV concept is understandably short on precise specs, which is the norm for military vehicle announcements. What we can infer , however, has massive potential for the electric truck market. Consider the following reported capabilities: a 102 kWh battery pack, silent electric drive, an onboard internal combustion engine (likely the same 186 hp, 2.8 liter GM Duramax four-cylinder turbo-diesel used in GM’s other Silverado-based military trucks) to recharge the battery and provide continuous V2L and V2G capabilities to equipment in the field.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That’s a ton of capability (sorry) packed into GM’s one-ton dually chassis – and it’s exactly the kind of work-ready EREV or PHEV pickup that America’s work-focused fleets, RVers, and truck enthusiasts have been begging for . And, as for whether or not the UGV really has a chance at seeing production, GM’s own people are hinting that this military concept isn’t a one-off.
“We do not begin with a blank sheet of paper,” said Steve duMont , president of GM Defense. “By transferring GM’s world-class engineering, supply chain and manufacturing scale directly to the service member, we are transforming customer needs into mission-ready capability faster than ever before.”
In addition to the hybrid 3500 chassis, other potential consumer breakthroughs include a more advanced autonomous system than we’ve yet seen in production-spec GM vehicles. The UGV was displayed with Scout AI’s Gx Ground Agent autonomy system, which uses an open, modular interface to accommodate different sensors and mission systems while subtly implying that the eyes-off ADAS scheduled to appear in 2028 under GM’s Super Cruise branding is also making significant progress.
So, is GM bringing full-size, body-on-frame, electric drive EREV 3500 dually pickup , with real hot-shot towing capabilities , and eyes-off ADAS to market in 2028 ? A boy can dream, can’t he? Let us know how that all sounds to you, in the comments.

Volvo EX60 beats EPA range in the real world
Volvo calls the EX60 a “game changer” as its fastest-charging, longest-range electric vehicle to date.
In July, Volvo announced the 2027 EX60 P10 AWD received an official EPA certification with an estimated driving range of up to 330 miles, beating its own estimate of 322 miles.
When fitted with the 22″ tires, the EX60 P10 AWD Ultra boasts an EPA-estimated range of 312 miles on a single charge.

During Edmunds recent EV Range Test , the AWD electric SUV proved it can drive further than advertised.
The EX60 P10 AWD (with 22″ tires) covered 352 miles on a single charge during the test, beating its EPA-estimated 312 miles by 13%.
Volvo’s electric SUV also outperformed many luxury competitors that underwent the same test, including the Cadillac Lyriq AWD (319 miles) and Mercedes-Benz EQS+ 320 SUV (349 miles). However, it wasn’t enough to beat Mercedes’ new GLC 400 EV, which managed 392 miles.
2027 Volvo EX60 (Source: Volvo)
It was also more efficient than expected, using just 28.8 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA-estimated 30 kWh per 100 miles.
The Edmunds EV Range Test is designed to offer a more accurate estimate of a vehicle’s range during real-world, everyday driving conditions. It consists of 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph.
Volvo EX60 interior (Source: Volvo)
The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set on auto at 72 degrees.
Measuring 189.1″ long, 81.4″ wide, and 64.4″ high, with a 116.9″ wheelbase, the EX60 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y.

Tesla’s proxy for its 2026 annual meeting, filed today, confirms that one of its supposedly independent directors now sits on SpaceX’s board. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs both Tesla’s compensation committee and its governance committee, joined SpaceX’s board in February.
That’s one of several details in the filing that line up with a Tesla-SpaceX merger. There’s a three-item ballot, an auto-voting program that kicks in for the next vote, and Musk pay terms that pay out on a deal price alone.
Three items, no shareholder proposals
Tesla’s 2026 annual meeting is set for December 3 at Gigafactory Texas, for shareholders of record as of October 13.
They get three things to vote on. The first is re-electing Elon Musk, board chair Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel to three-year terms. The second is a non-binding say-on-pay vote, and the third is ratifying PwC as Tesla’s auditor, a job it has held since 2005.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That’s it. No shareholder proposals made the ballot this year. At least, not yet. Last year’s meeting featured several, including one asking the board to invest in xAI, which has since been absorbed by SpaceX.
The board also says it won’t bring back proposals to declassify itself or to drop Tesla’s supermajority voting requirements. Its 2025 attempt drew 73.6% participation but only 39.4% of outstanding shares in support, short of the bar. So the staggered board stays, and the three directors up this year would serve until 2029.
Denholm’s letter makes the pitch directly, telling shareholders that “a steady and experienced hand during this time of rapid technological change is essential to Tesla’s success.”
As chair, Denholm has long been criticized for letting Elon Musk do what he wants, unchecked by the board, but with Musk’s backing, it’s doubtful Tesla shareholders can get her out.
Musk’s 2025 pay: $158 billion on paper
The say-on-pay item asks shareholders to approve Musk’s 2025 compensation, which the proxy reports at $158,359,009,867. Against a median Tesla employee who made $62,786, that’s a CEO pay ratio of 2,522,203 to 1.
None of that was cash. The figure combines $132.3 billion for the 2025 CEO Performance Award, valued as if every milestone gets hit, and $26.1 billion for the August 2025 “interim award.” Musk forfeited the interim award in April after the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated his 2018 package.
Tesla adds its own “realized compensation” table showing Musk received $0 in 2025, for a pay ratio of “0.00:1.” Accurate for 2025. But the same proxy discloses that on June 16, 2026, Musk exercised all 303,960,630 of his 2018 options, covering the $23.34 exercise price by having Tesla withhold 17,531,857 shares. That implies a share price of about $405 and a value of roughly $116 billion at exercise.
Tesla’s income statement tells a third story. The 2025 award has generated $689 million in stock-based compensation expense so far: $162 million in 2025 and $527 million in the first half of 2026. Tesla only books expense for milestones it considers “probable,” and out of 12 operational milestones it rates exactly one as probable: 20 million cumulative vehicle deliveries.
FSD subscriptions, Optimus, robotaxis and every EBITDA target sit in the “not probable” bucket, worth $105.8 billion to $120.4 billion in unrecognized expense.
All of this comes after a year where Tesla’s net income fell 46% to $3.86 billion and revenue declined for a second straight year, to $94.8 billion.
How a merger pays Musk
As we noted when Tesla got the SEC’s OK to auto-vote retail shares , the 2025 award works differently in a change in control. The filings lay out exactly how.
Normally, each of the 12 tranches needs a market cap milestone, measured as a trailing average over six months and 30 days, plus an operational milestone. In a change in control, operational milestones drop out. Tesla’s market cap gets measured once: shares outstanding multiplied by the higher of the last closing price or the per-share value shareholders receive in the deal. Any tranche earned that way vests immediately instead of after 7.5 to 10 years.
With 3.95 billion shares outstanding, the first $2 trillion tranche works out to about $506 per share. A deal valuing Tesla at $3 trillion, or about $759 per share, would earn Musk three tranches, or 105.9 million shares, without a single robotaxi or Optimus milestone.
The April 2026 Implementation Agreement for the 2018 package follows the same logic. The 286.4 million restricted shares Musk received from the June exercise don’t vest until January 19, 2028. A change in control while he’s still CEO, or running product or operations, vests them right away.
Whether a Tesla-SpaceX combination would count as a change in control depends on how it’s structured. But both of Musk’s packages are now built to pay out fast if it does.
The auto-vote button arrives
This meeting is also the launch of Tesla’s “Voluntary Retail Voting Program.” Retail shareholders who vote through ProxyVote or Robinhood will be offered enrollment in a standing instruction for all future meetings.
There are two options. The first votes your shares with the board on everything. The second votes with the board on everything except a “Special Matter,” which Tesla defines as a contested director election or a merger, acquisition or divestiture that needs shareholder approval.
There’s no option to vote against the board. Shareholders who pick “all matters” will have their shares counted for the board’s position on a merger unless they log in and override it. Tesla’s only commitment is a reminder before that meeting.
The instructions don’t apply to the December 3 vote. They start with the next shareholder meeting, which is where a SpaceX deal would land.
Three of nine directors tied to SpaceX
Ehrenpreis isn’t the only link. Elon Musk runs SpaceX, and his brother Kimbal Musk, also a Tesla director, has served on SpaceX’s board. That’s a third of Tesla’s nine-member board.
Tesla’s board still classifies Ehrenpreis as independent. As chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, his job description includes “considering questions of possible conflicts of interest of Tesla’s directors and officers.”
Tesla is also a SpaceX shareholder now. Its $2 billion investment in xAI converted into SpaceX Class A stock after SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings in February, and the purchase closed on March 12. The SpaceX S-1 put that stake at 18,990,195 shares , under 1% of the company.
The money flows the other way too. Tesla’s proxy shows $430.1 million in 2025 revenue from xAI, mostly Megapacks, and another $143.3 million from SpaceX, mostly vehicles.
On the Q2 earnings call in July , Musk said a combination would have to “be done with the appropriate process.”
Electrek’s Take
Ehrenpreis has been on Tesla’s board since 2007. The 2018 changes came out of the Tornetta mess. And the auto-vote program is sold as a fix for low retail turnout.

Put them side by side, though, and it reads like a checklist for a merger vote. Musk’s pay packages pay out quickly on a deal price. The director in charge of reviewing conflicts sits on the other company’s board. The board that would negotiate the deal is locked in through 2029. And retail shareholders are being offered a button that turns them into standing votes for the board, merger included, unless they pick the carve-out.
The problem is who’s on the other side of the table. Musk owns about 20% of Tesla and controls roughly 85% of SpaceX’s voting power. Whatever exchange ratio the two boards land on, he benefits from both ends of it. That’s exactly when Tesla shareholders need the most independent board possible. Instead, the board is getting closer to SpaceX, not further away.
Musk is right that this needs “the appropriate process,” but of course, he doesn’t really mean it. He has engineered Tesla’s board and shareholder base for years to answer to one person: him.

This Classic Ford F-250 Highboy Is a Nostalgic Throwback to Old-School Truck Camping
8 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Truck camping is very popular today, with many people considering that the same vehicle that gets them through the work week can also take them down rough roads and into the middle of nowhere without the need for a separate adventure vehicle. But the idea of turning a pickup into an adventure rig is nothing new.
People have been exploring the outdoors and camping out of their work trucks for decades, and today, I’m going to cast a light on a vintage truck camper that evokes nostalgia and exudes the undeniable charm associated with older, simpler times. This is a 1976 Ford F-250 Highboy pickup truck with a vintage slide-in camper that proves truck camping has been around for generations and that things were much simpler back in the day. This unique rig has now come up for sale and is offered with a 1978 Honda XL125 motorcycle mounted at the front.
The base for this camper is a rare, period-correct Ford F-250 Highboy from 1976, which is still powered by its original 360-cubic-inch V8 and retains its four-speed manual transmission and divorced transfer case. Basically, the three-quarter-ton 4x4 has the mechanical configuration that made the Highboy a distinctive part of Ford’s truck lineup.
The vehicle is part of a special batch of F-Series Ford pickups built from 1967 until early 1977. Featuring a narrower F-3530 frame, factory four-wheel-drive, and a divorced transfer case mounted separately on the frame, they were nicknamed Highboys by enthusiasts.
Photo: Mecum Auctions This was never an official factory designation, but the moniker stuck through the years, having been earned because the divorced transfer case was not mounted directly to the transmission but separately in the middle of the truck, requiring extra clearance, which prompted Ford to add a factory rear lift block and a taller front suspension setup. Due to this configuration, Highboys sit five to six inches (12 to 15 cm) higher than standard models straight from the factory.
Ford eventually reworked the four-wheel-drive setup on the F-250 and switched to a transfer case mounted to the transmission midway through the 1977 model year. The subsequent trucks were fitted with slightly lower suspension and became known as, you guessed it, “Lowboys.”
It’s also worth mentioning that, by 1976, when the unit featured here left the factory, the pickup truck had received several improvements over its earlier versions, including front disc brakes on regular-cab models.
Apart from its period-correct drivetrain, this Ford F-250 Highboy also preserves its original exterior appearance, which stands out with the Free Wheeling decal kit. Ford launched the Free Wheeling graphics option in 1977 for F-Series trucks. It featured multi-colored chromatic "sunset" gradient stripes in red, orange, and yellow, combined with blacked-out grilles, headlight surrounds, and black bumpers, along with special sport mirrors and optional rolling packages.
Photo: Mecum Auctions But according to historical registry data, the Free Wheeling option was produced in very low numbers on heavy-duty three-quarter-ton trucks, which makes this F-250 even more special.
As you can see in the attached picture gallery, the pickup truck’s exterior clearly shows the signs of the inevitable flow of time, but this example’s rust patina has been clear-coated, locking in the aged, weathered look of old paint and oxidized metal. This, combined with the Free Wheeling decal, gives the Ford the look of a genuine recreational vehicle assembled in the 1970s.
Speaking of its RV persona, the pickup has been fitted with a vintage Wolverine Pup camper. This is a classic slide-in truck camper produced by Wolverine Campers, a popular manufacturer from the 1950s through the late 1980s. Unfortunately, the listing doesn’t include any photos of its interior, but these compact, lightweight slide-in units often included basic living quarters.
The Pup mounted on the bed of this truck has a rear entrance and a pair of small windows on each side, but we know nothing about its interior layout, so we can only assume it’s a convertible kind of living space since there is no cab-over section to hold the bed.
Photo: Mecum Auctions Another noteworthy feature on the outside is a custom front bumper that accommodates a rare Warn 8274 winch. Perfect for self-recovery in difficult situations, this particular detail is another indication of the vehicle’s intended recreational use.
This vintage camper is offered with a 1978 Honda XL125, a small-displacement motorcycle suited to recreational riding. Carried on a custom front mount, it offers a glimpse into how daredevils used to outfit their trucks for camping and outdoor adventures decades ago. Together, the Ford truck, slide-in camper, and motorcycle make up a complete, turn-key vintage overlanding setup.
Classic Ford F-250 Highboy pickup trucks are highly sought after by collectors, and this particular example truly stands out for its original drivetrain, vintage graphics, and period-correct equipment. The truck, together with the Wolverine Pup camper and the Honda motorcycle, is scheduled to cross the auction block with Mecum in late October.

Western Boxy SUVs with Round Headlights Have a New Player to Worry About: The iCAUR V25
21 photos
Photo: iCAUR
There is something about square-bodied SUVs with round headlights that immediately makes my skin tingle, but in a good way. Just picture the Ford Bronco, or the G-Class, or the newer Land Rovers.
The design targets a particular segment of the population: people who can afford to go off-roading in a vehicle that looks different, is very capable, and, if possible, packs as many luxurious features as possible.
Until recently, carmakers executing such designs had nothing to fear from Chinese carmakers, as they didn’t really seem interested in going after buyers in this segment. Something changed recently, so the world now has to deal with such vehicles made by the likes of Jetour and iCAUR.
It’s the latter that’s of interest to us today, as it has announced the official public debut of the mid-size V25 SUV. Ok, the design has been in the news for a while now, but it is this week that the company presented it in front of a public audience during the iCAUR International User Summit that took place in Wuhu, China.
As a reminder, iCAUR (which is also known as iCAR, which in turn is short for iCar Ecological Technology) is an offshoot of Chery International, and it has already tested the waters of carmaking with products the likes of the 03, V23, and V27.
An electrified SUV by trade, the V25 is joining the party as the company’s first product to target international markets in an organized fashion. It has already been confirmed as a player on the Australian market, and it will probably expand elsewhere pretty fast.
I said earlier that the established boxy SUVs in the Western world have a new player to worry about, and I really mean that. Design-wise, at least, as the way the V25 has been made to look is at the same time familiar and fresh, old-school and original, retro and futuristic.
As far as performance levels go, things look pretty decent as well, at least on paper. The SUV relies on a range extender system that blends together a 1.5-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder internal combustion engine rated at 154 hp that feeds electricity into a lithium-ion battery pack good for 93 miles (150 km, as measured under WLTC) on a single fill.
The company is probably using the land Down Under as a sort of test market for the future, and for now it did not confirm the arrival of the mid-size SUV on the European market. The UK will see the first iCAUR product in the form of the larger, flagship V27, which is scheduled to enter the local market early next year.
We’ll keep an eye on that, and also on the other exploits of this new car company, and report back once we know more.

Miami-based cargo airline Amerijet International plans to repair a 36-year-old Boeing 767-300 converted freighter aircraft that suffered fuselage damage from a hard landing in Guatemala City last month, CEO Joe Mozzali said.
The aircraft’s age left many speculating that it wasn’t worth fixing and would be scrapped for parts, but Mozzali said Amerijet’s insurance company will cover the cost of the repair because it is less expensive than paying a claim for an aircraft declared totally damaged.
In reality, even badly damaged freighter aircraft are too valuable to part with because of the current shortage of widebody freighters, supply chain challenges that are slowing passenger-to-freighter conversions and limited feedstock caused by passenger airlines holding longer onto aircraft because engine-quality problems are slowing delivery of new aircraft, according to air cargo experts.
Amerijet has hired a local repair station to conduct a temporary repair in Guatemala City and will then ferry the aircraft to a maintenance facility for a longer-term repair, Mozzali told FreightWaves in an email exchange. It is uncertain when the plane will be ready to return to service.
The Amerijet aircraft departed Miami on Sept. 6 and landed hard on its nose gear first, resulting in buckle damage to the top of the fuselage, according to The Aviation Herald and photos on social media. The aircraft has remained grounded at Guatemala City International Airport since the incident.

Aviation safety experts say “skin buckling” can occur when the structure beneath the skin, including ribs and load-bearing beams, is distorted or bent. 10 photos
Photo: UK Barn Finds/YouTube
When it comes to British classics, we often get excited about Jaguars, Aston Martins , Rolls-Royces, and Bentleys. And that makes sense; petrolheads have a thing for sports cars and luxury vehicles. But needless to say, the original Mini Cooper also has a cult following.
However, the British automotive heritage extends far beyond the aforementioned brands and nameplates. We also have old Land Rovers, as well as carmakers like Lotus, Triumph, and MG. The Elan, TR6, and MGB definitely deserve spots in the automotive hall of fame, as do the Ford Cortina and Escort. However, some cars don't get as much attention as they should outside the UK. The Morris Minor is one of them.
The Minor was produced by Morris Motors Limited, which was established in 1919. The company merged with Austin to form the British Motor Corporation (BMC) in 1952, but the Morris name remained in use until 1984. Designed by Alec Issigonis, who also penned the Mini Cooper, the Minor is the company's most famous car.
The Morris Minor debuted in 1948, replacing the Eight. It was one of Britain's first post-WW2 designs. Measuring only 148 inches (3,759 mm) long, the Minor arrived with features that were ahead of their time for an economy car, including rack-and-pinion steering and independent suspension. Its low price and affordable maintenance made it quite popular in post-war Britain.
Morris sold one million units by late 1960 and a total of 1.6 million examples until the nameplate was discontinued in 1971. Body styles included a two-door sedan, a four-door sedan, a two-door convertible, and a two-door wagon. The Minor received notable upgrades in 1952, 1956, and 1962. All cars were powered by small-displacement four-cylinder engines.
Despite the massive production number, the Morris Minor is a rare sight today. How so? Well, for starters, it was treated as a throw-away vehicle; most Minors were dumped into junkyards. Second, these cars aren't worth much today, so fully restored vehicles aren't common outside the Morris Minor fan club.
And sadly enough, very few Minors get rescued nowadays. Most of them have become rust buckets and barely provide useful parts for ongoing projects. The example you see here is one of the many Minors that sat for decades, but unlike its siblings, it's still (mostly) in one piece. And it was also lucky enough to get a revival.
The car had been parked in a backyard in 1989, and it almost became one with the bushes in 37 years. Our host says that the rescue was unintentional; the Morris was purchased only because it came as a package deal with another vehicle he wanted from the property. Fortunately, that didn't stop the buyer from cleaning it and getting the engine running again.
And while the car looked damaged beyond salvation, the old inline-four agreed to run again without much intervention. And amazingly enough, it was still capable of moving the Minor around. The car is obviously too rusty to be revived with reasonable costs, but it's cool to see it driving after so many decades off the road.
This Minor is a Series III, also known as the Minor 1000 . This version debuted in 1956 and remained in production until 1971, with nearly 850,000 units made. How can you tell it apart from older Minors? Well, the front grille is the obvious hint; it's wider at the top and has horizontal slats. Hit the play button below to see it coming back to life.

Would a carrier really design its Asia-Europe network around shaving marginal ETS dollars, which it can recoup through surcharges anyway?
In short, carriers did redesign for the ETS – though not around the ETS alone.
Carriers have redesigned Asia–Europe loops to cut their exposure, and they were right to. But the money is not marginal, a surcharge does not make it someone else’s problem, and carbon was never the first reason to call Britain first. Those ports suit the ships; the EU Emissions Trading System made a good choice better.
A few months ago, the EU ETS Observatory published a report stating that UK volume growth was a direct result of shippers seeking to minimise the EU-ETS charges – bullocks, if you ask me.
Container Trade Statistics (CTS), which counts laden boxes by origin and destination, has UK trade up 3% in 2025, against 5% for North Europe as a whole: the Netherlands grew 6%, France 5%, Poland 18%. Britain grew, but slower than its neighbours.
Source: Container Trades Statistics
For a carrier to reduce its exposure is not just an operational saving, it is a commercial competitive advantage: the less your “Carbon surcharge” is, the more attractive your all-in freight charge – you certainly don’t want to be the most expensive in the market.
How a first call is chosen
A rotation is built from constraints before costs: transit time; maximum draught and air draught; the number of cranes and how far and high they reach; the volume each port generates; rail and road links inland; and berth windows that fit the schedule. Only then does the voyage costing run; fuel, port charges, charter hire and, since 2024, carbon. Together they make up the unit cost.
Source: Solvens Advisory
The first call in North Europe is the most demanding, because the ship arrives from Asia at its deepest draught. Few terminals take a 24,000 teu vessel at full scantling draught without restriction: Rotterdam, Felixstowe, and London Gateway can. Antwerp or Southampton take the same ships, but with draught limits. Wilhelmshaven has the water, but calling there first adds transit time to every port after it.
Put Felixstowe or London Gateway first and nothing is lost; the ship has the water, UK importers get the fastest transit, and almost no nautical deviation means the next port is served swiftly thereafter.
Taking the Asia leg out of the ETS as well is a win-win, and carriers took it deliberately.
The test to come
Sea-Intelligence Consulting found the 2026 networks cut ETS-chargeable distance by another 11%. This is simply optimisation, and cost nothing operationally. The evolution of Gemini’s AE3 shows this – Algeciras out at both ends, London Gateway first, and Southampton last – presented by Hapag-Lloyd as ‘enhanced Baltic coverage’ and better for UK exports. Both are true.
Brussels now proposes that container ports with deepsea infrastructure, within 150 nautical miles of the EU, no longer count as a break in the voyage. Felixstowe, London Gateway, and Southampton would qualify. Carriers would pay more, but it is doubtul the rotations would change: the ships still need the water, and Rotterdam still has no spare berths.
That makes the listing a useful experiment. If Britain mostly stays first, once the carbon reward has gone, the leakage thesis will be buried once and for all.
A tax that barely decarbonises
Step back, and the UK first-call says something less comfortable about the ETS itself. In shipping, its effectiveness has been limited, for at least two reasons.
The first is above – carriers optimised their networks within the rules, as they were entitled to, and importers were spared hundreds of millions of euros a year: the Observatory puts the allowances not collected at the three UK ports alone at about €316m. But the deeper cost is not the revenue. A UK first-call does not change a ship’s emissions: same ship, same miles. It removes the carbon price from the Asia leg, the longest of the voyage, and with it any ETS reason to slow down or burn a bio-blend there. The price signal, which is the point of the scheme, stops at the Channel .
The second is where the money goes. Shipping now pays for all its in-scope emissions, roughly 90m tonnes, about €7bn a year at €80. Since 2023, member states have been asked to spend all ETS revenue on climate and energy, and in 2024 they reported 80%. But climate is not shipping. The commission’s carbon market report found about 5% of national ETS revenue went to industrial decarbonisation, and only France and Estonia ringfence a share for shipping. The Innovation Fund holds 20m allowances for maritime projects over 2024–2030, about €1.6bn in all, against a bill of €7bn a year.
In other words, the industry pays for a transition it barely gets to finance.
Brussels has noticed. Its July proposal would create a reserve of up to 110m allowances from 2028 to 2040, covering 55%–90% of the price gap for sustainable fuels and zero-emission propulsion. Per tonne of green fuel, that is generous. In total it is about €0.7bn a year, a tenth of what shipping pays, and if claims exceed it, every claim is cut.
FuelEU Maritime shows the alternative. Its compliance cost stays inside the industry: a ship that over-complies pools its surplus with one that falls short, and the money moves from one shipowner to another that has invested in cleaner fuel. The ETS takes the same industry’s money to national treasuries and asks it to decarbonise anyway.
Carriers do not design networks around the ETS. They design them around ships, water and berths, then cut the carbon bill wherever the network allows, and compete on the surcharge that results. A scheme that taxes legs rather than trades, and spends the proceeds elsewhere, invited exactly that.
If Brussels wants carbon cut, rather than collected, the next revision should worry less about Felixstowe and way more about where the money goes.

The BYD makes it happen thanks to its DiSus-P Ultra hydraulic suspension, which takes active body control way beyond the usual “ride and handling” bit by allowing the plug-in SUV to independently raise or lower each corner up to 300 mm (~11.5 inches) with a lifting capacity of up to nine metric tons (~a lot).

source_document.body:
Hitachi Energy will invest more than $330 million in a new transformer insulation factory in London, Ontario. The project will bring production of a key material used inside transformers to Canada for the first time.
What’s Related
The 226,000-square-foot facility is expected to be completed by 2028 and create more than 100 jobs . It will manufacture electrical insulation pressboard and laminates for transformer production.
The factory will establish Canada’s first pressboard manufacturing line and Hitachi Energy’s first in the Americas. Planned annual output is up to 20,000 metric tons, with materials going to the company’s transformer operations in Varennes, Quebec, and other manufacturers in North America and overseas.
Federal and provincial governments are contributing up to approximately $35.3 million toward the project. That includes about $21.2 million from the Canadian government and up to $14.1 million from Ontario.
What is pressboard?
Pressboard is an insulation material made from wood fiber. Inside transformers, it provides electrical insulation and helps with cooling, so its quality and consistency affect how well the equipment works and how long it lasts.
The London facility will use four machines called formers, which shape wet pulp into sheets. Ontario says it will be the world's first transformer pressboard factory with four of these machines.
Located in London’s Huron Industrial Park, the plant will use manufacturing technology and automation to turn wood fiber into finished insulation materials. The federal government says the project will source key inputs locally, creating business for Canadian suppliers, including pulp producers.
“This investment reflects our long-term commitment to Canadian industry, talent and innovation in an electric economy ,” said Carla Vicente, country managing director of Hitachi Energy Canada.
Loosening up a bottleneck
Hitachi Energy says limited supplies of specialized insulation materials remain a bottleneck for transformer manufacturers. The new plant is intended to bring production closer to North American customers as electricity demand grows.
The announcement identifies industrial projects, AI and data centers, expanding communities, and electrification as sources of that demand. The factory will supply materials needed to build the transformers that serve those projects.
“This project demonstrates that there are high-value opportunities for forest products in critical energy infrastructure ,” said Tim Hodgson, Canada’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.
Building on investments in Ontario and Quebec
The project follows Hitachi Energy’s June announcement of an agreement to acquire Canduct Group, an Ontario-based manufacturer of transformer insulation kits and components. Canduct serves equipment manufacturers and repair companies in the United States and Canada and has supplied Hitachi Energy for more than 20 years.
Hitachi Energy also announced a $195 million expansion in Varennes in September 2025. That project is intended to nearly triple the site’s large power transformer production, while the new London factory will supply insulation materials to those operations.
